name: Angolan Muamba de Galinha
description: Muamba de galinha is Angola's national dish, and despite sharing a name with Congolese moambe, real Angolan muamba is built differently - it skips peanuts entirely, getting its nutty depth purely from real red palm oil, with butternut squash and okra as genuine, defining vegetables, not optional additions. Real technique marinates the chicken in lemon and garlic first, then browns it in the palm oil before the vegetables go in.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the lemon juice and garlic for at least 15 minutes.
Brown the chicken in the palm oil, 6-7 minutes.
Add the onion, tomatoes, and jalapeño, and cook 4-5 minutes.
Add the squash and enough water to just cover, and simmer 20 minutes until the squash is nearly tender.
Add the okra and simmer 8-10 minutes more, until the chicken and squash are both fully tender and the sauce has thickened from the okra.

name: Angolan Funge
description: Funge, a stiff cassava or cornmeal porridge, is Angola's most essential staple starch, traditionally the accompaniment to muamba de galinha, real technique beating it hard while cooking to build a smooth, cohesive dough rather than a lumpy mush.
steps_detailed: Whisk about a third of the cornmeal with the salt into 1.25 cups boiling water.
Gradually beat in the remaining cornmeal, stirring vigorously and continuously, over medium-low heat 15-18 minutes, until very thick, smooth, and pulls away from the sides of the pot.

name: Angolan Piri Piri Chicken
description: Frango à moda de Angola (piri piri chicken), grilled chicken basted in a fiery chili sauce, reflects real Portuguese colonial influence merged with African chili, real technique basting continuously through grilling rather than just at the start.
steps_detailed: Blend the jalapeño, garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil into a smooth sauce.
Marinate the chicken in the sauce at least 30 minutes.
Grill, turning and basting with more sauce every few minutes, 12-15 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Angolan Kizaka
description: Kizaka, pounded cassava leaves cooked with palm oil, is a genuine Angolan staple - real cassava leaves aren't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for a milder, less fibrous approximation.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion and garlic in the palm oil 3-4 minutes.
Add the spinach and a splash of water, and simmer 12-15 minutes until well combined and tender.
